S065.name: Obsessions
S065.description: Recurrent and persistent thoughts, urges, or images that are experienced as intrusive and unwanted, and attempts to ignore or suppress them.

subtypes.Contamination Obsessions: Recurrent and intrusive worries about contamination, germs, or dirt.
subtypes.Pathological Doubt: Pathological doubt regarding safety or mistakes, such as whether doors are locked or gas valves are closed.
subtypes.Symmetry and Exactness Obsessions: A strong urge that items must be lined up exactly or be symmetrical.
subtypes.Forbidden or Taboo Thoughts: Intrusive thoughts involving aggressive (harming others), sexual, or religious content that are prohibited.
subtypes.Somatic Obsessions: Persistent and specific fear that one might have a serious disease.

S066.name: Compulsions
S066.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to an obsession or to prevent anxiety/distress; clearly excessive or not realistically connected.

subtypes.Cleaning or Washing Compulsions: Repetitive acts to remove contamination, such as hand washing, showering, or excessive cleaning.
subtypes.Checking Compulsions: Repeatedly checking items like door locks, gas stoves, or switches to prevent danger.
subtypes.Ordering and Arranging Compulsions: Organizing objects in a specific order or at a precise angle to reduce anxiety.
subtypes.Mental Acts: Mental rituals performed internally, such as praying, counting, or repeating specific words silently.
subtypes.Repeating Rituals: Repeating specific actions (e.g., standing up, passing through a door) a set number of times.

patient_info.stressor_event: Major change in responsibilities at work (e.g., promotion, demotion)
patient_info.stressor: Kennetra was given expanded month-end reconciliation duties at her bookkeeping firm after a senior clerk left, and she took pride in being trusted with accounts that affected payroll, vendors, and tax reporting. Under the new responsibility, early perfectionistic double-checking evolved into intrusive, unwanted thoughts that a hidden error would harm the firm or its clients, followed by repeated spreadsheet reviews and mental calculations that no longer matched the actual level of risk. Over an unclear period, the cycle became severely impairing: she stayed late, missed choir rehearsals and youth-center commitments, and still could not reliably release completed work on time. After a missed filing deadline led to a formal workplace meeting, she used the company’s employee assistance referral to arrange psychiatric care.

S065.name: Obsessions
S065.description: Recurrent and persistent thoughts, urges, or images that are experienced as intrusive and unwanted, and attempts to ignore or suppress them.
S065.manifestation: Even after I know the numbers match, this thought keeps jumping in that I missed one hidden mistake in payroll or taxes and somebody's check won't go through or the firm will get in trouble, and I try to push it away but it comes right back like I can't trust my own eyes.

S066.name: Compulsions
S066.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to an obsession or to prevent anxiety/distress; clearly excessive or not realistically connected.
S066.manifestation: I'm here because I can't stop going back over the same spreadsheets and calculations again and again, sometimes staying at work for hours after everyone leaves, even when I already checked them, because if I don't do it one more time I feel like something bad will happen and it'll be my fault.

functional_impairment.name: Functional Impairment
functional_impairment.manifestation: I missed a filing deadline and got called into a formal meeting at work, and I’ve stopped making it to choir rehearsals and youth-center commitments because I can’t get out of the office on time.
